gate_answer.question: Does any row grade Grade-A AND fluid simultaneously?
gate_answer.answer: YES -- on exactly one row, R1 = arXiv:2509.25116 (Hou, Wang, Yang).
gate_answer.reading_a_applied: Per pre-committed reading (a), the YES is reported FIRST and unsoftened, and is recorded as SOMEONE ELSE FILLED THE CELL. That is NOT this repository moving a link. No link of the L1->L4 chain moves. Clay odds stay ~0.05%.
gate_answer.the_qualification_that_must_travel_with_: R1's certified object is NOT a finite-time singularity. It is a FORWARD self-similar Leray-Hopf profile, and the paper says so in its own words (Section 1.2, p.2): 'The readers should not confuse this self-similar setting, which starts from singular initial data, with the backward self-similar setting related to finite-time singularities from smooth initial data.' Theorem 1's solutions are 'smooth for positive times'. Leg 174's criterion, as quoted in PUB_0C_CENSUS_SPINE §1 and as handed to this leg, has exactly TWO clauses and does not contain a finite-time-singularity clause. Adding one would be TIGHTENING the criterion, which the dispatch forbids. So the YES stands as graded, and the qualification is recorded beside it rather than used to withdraw it. WALLS.md's 'BREAKING W3 CONSISTS OF' paragraph DOES contain a third requirement ('the object is a genuine finite-time singularity') that R1 does not meet. That divergence between the wall's break-test and the criterion the wall names as its own predicate is a BAN-WORDING DEFECT and is escalated to the user, NOT ruled by this leg.
